Winery

Edoardo Miroglio

A winery in south-eastern Bulgaria, at Elenovo near Nova Zagora, created by the Piedmontese businessman Edoardo Miroglio. It makes reds from international and native varieties, such as Mavrud, and traditional-method sparkling wines.

The Edoardo Miroglio winery was born in the early 2000s on the initiative of Edoardo Miroglio, a textile businessman from Piedmont, in northern Italy, who decided to invest in Bulgarian vineyards. It is one of the best-known examples of the arrival of foreign capital in Bulgarian wine after the end of the planned economy, and brings to the country an outlook shaped by the Italian wine tradition.

The winery and its vineyards are near the village of Elenovo, close to Nova Zagora, in the eastern part of the great Thracian plain. The estate was planted with international varieties such as Pinot Noir, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah, together with Bulgarian varieties such as Mavrud and Rubin, and some whites.

Production combines varietal and blended reds, among them a Mavrud red that shows the character of this native grape, with Pinot Noir wines, a variety unusual in southern Bulgaria that has become one of the house’s hallmarks. The winery also makes traditional-method sparkling wines, with second fermentation in bottle, a speciality that is rare in the country. The style aims for reds with ripe fruit and balanced structure, with barrel ageing in the higher ranges, and wines that combine the ripeness of the Thracian climate with the freshness brought by the varieties and by the early picking of grapes intended for sparkling wine.
